title: Ben Johnson discusses Mike Ditka's impact on Bears | Press Conference
headline: Kyle Monangai is out this week with a toe injury, which should push more work to Roschon Johnson; D'Andre Swift is expected to play Sunday but his workload is unsettled.
summary: Johnson opened by honoring Mike Ditka, calling him the gold standard for the franchise and saying he is humbled to hold the same job. In answering questions he described Ditka's impact as a player, a coach, and a figure whose photos hang throughout Halas Hall, and tied the 1980s defense to the 'Monsters of the Midway' standard. On the injury front, Kyle Monangai's toe injury turned out to be more serious than first thought, so he will not play this week and is in a boot while specialists evaluate him; he is week to week and not an IR candidate. Johnson said the rest of the group is trending well for availability. He called the red zone and finishing drives the team's biggest offensive problem and said the fix is heightened focus and clearer calls. He praised Roschon Johnson as a complete back who is likely to see a bigger role with Monangai out, and said Swift is in a good spot to help this weekend, though he would not commit to a specific workload split. Caleb Williams is on track in his hamstring recovery, with a throwing progression in place, and no return date has been set. Johnson also said the team will likely elevate one player from the practice squad to the 53-man roster this weekend.

Recovering from a hamstring injury; on track, progressing through a throwing protocol, return timeline to be determined.

topics.detail: Johnson spoke about Mike Ditka's legacy as a player and coach, including his 11 seasons, Super Bowl win, and influence on the team's tough identity.
Johnson called red zone and drive-finishing issues the main offensive concern and said the fix is more focus and clearer communication, with no single solution.
The team will likely elevate one practice-window player to the 53-man roster this weekend, now that a spot is open. The player was not named.
The team discussed the long history with Green Bay as motivation for the matchup, and Johnson planned to talk about Ditka with the team.

title: Jim Harbaugh Remembers Mike Ditka & Gives Injury Updates
headline: Harbaugh gave no firm word on WR Quentin Johnston's chest injury for Sunday vs. Denver, and offered only a vague 'yes' on his availability; OL Rashawn Slater's surgery reportedly went well with no return timeline.
summary: Harbaugh opened by remembering Mike Ditka, calling him an American original and a man of faith, family and football, and describing how Ditka treated his players and their families like his own. He shared a story of Ditka quietly writing $500 checks to people in need while they were meeting about the game plan, noting Ditka never sought credit for it. On the offensive line, Harbaugh said fans would see on Sunday how the unit is deployed, hinting that some version of the group that finished the last game could return. Asked about Rashawn Slater, he said he had not spoken to him since surgery, just before it, but understood the procedure was successful; he did not give a timeline. When asked whether Quentin Johnston's chest injury would be a factor in Sunday's game, Harbaugh answered 'Yes, yes,' which is ambiguous and does not clearly confirm whether Johnston will play. The Chargers face the Denver Broncos on Sunday.

injuries.detail: Chest injury. Harbaugh's 'Yes, yes' answer to whether it is in play for Sunday was ambiguous; no clear status given.
Underwent surgery; Harbaugh understood it was successful but gave no return timeline or availability update.

signals.claim: Chest injury may or may not keep him out Sunday vs. Denver; availability not clearly confirmed
signals.note: Johnston's status for Sunday is unresolved, so his weekly fantasy projection should be treated as uncertain until the final injury report.

signals.claim: Surgery was successful per Harbaugh, but no return timeline was given
signals.note: Slater is an offensive lineman, so his absence or return affects blocking depth more than direct fantasy value.

topics.detail: Harbaugh said the Sunday game will show how the offensive line is deployed, and that the group which finished the last game may appear in some variation.
Harbaugh spoke at length about Mike Ditka's passing, calling him a mentor and a great man whose legacy he admired.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 9, 2026
headline: Goedert looked good in his return to practice, Dontayvion Wicks is expected to practice after a practice-report appearance, and Willie Lampkin and Jake Majors are set to be involved at guard/center.
summary: Sirianni said the week of preparation has gone well and that the locker room is locked in after the Jurgens trade, which he framed as a loss he will miss but one the team has moved past. He said the offensive line is a close-knit group that is getting back to work, with no change to the message. On the lineup, he expressed strong confidence in Willie Lampkin and Jake Majors, saying both had strong camps and played well in preseason reps, and that the coaches are game-planning around what the players do best. He said Dallas Goedert had a good week of practice and looked good back on the field, and that Drew Kendall has steadily improved and is a smart, hard-working player. On Dontayvion Wicks, he said he is expected to be at practice that day but that they would see where he is at the end of the day. He said the team is looking closely at the rise in soft-tissue injuries and trying to find solutions while managing the long season. He praised Dameon Pierce's energy, talent and work ethic and said he is excited for his opportunity. On Jacksonville, he called the Jaguars well coached and productive, noting their strong turnover differential, their tackling and ball pursuit, and Trevor Lawrence's play, and said the Eagles must play their best game.

title: Todd Bowles: Zyon McCollum ‘Playing Like An All-Pro’ | Press Conference
headline: Baker Mayfield's hand injury points to Jalon Daniels starting vs. the Steelers, while Bucky Irving and Zyon McCollum earned high praise.
summary: Bowles said Bucky Irving brought a different energy and a determined mindset, and credited the offensive line for his 72-yard run and closing 22-yard carry. He praised the corners, calling Zyon McCollum 'playing like an all pro corner right now' and noting Jacob Parrish's deflections, though Parrish tired and sat a play or two. McCollum's improvement was attributed to more film study on formations, splits, and down-and-distance. On Baker Mayfield, Bowles said the grip was smaller and he would know more later in the week, but the plan is to start Jalon Daniels against Pittsburgh. Daniels had only a few days to prepare on a short week and played within himself, and Bowles said he played smart and decisive. Bowles said Rueben Bain returned from missing games and looked good, needing to knock off some technique rust. He called the pressure from the front the best of the season even without sacks. Bowles acknowledged the offensive line's penalties have been creeping up each week and must be cleaned up. On Sean Tucker, Bowles said third-back usage depends on the hot hand, and Tucker would get more work if Irving cooled off. Bowles took responsibility for going for it on fourth-and-goal instead of kicking a field goal, calling it his decision.
